title: Council of Europe establishes the Register of Damage for Ukraine
body:
On 17 May 2023 the Council of Europe announced the creation of the Register of Damage for Ukraine at its heads of state summit in Reykjavik, Iceland. The Register is intended to serve as a record of evidence of damage, loss and injury caused to victims of Russia's crimes of aggression in Ukraine, and the Council said it would pave the way for a future international compensation mechanism.

The Register has its office in The Hague, with a satellite office in Ukraine. Forty-three countries and the European Union joined or said they intended to join at the time of the announcement, according to the Kyiv Independent.

Council of Europe Secretary General Marija Pejcinovic Buric called the Register a historic achievement and said that every loss would be counted and every damage compensated. Ukrainian Prime Minister Denys Shmyhal thanked the Council and participating states and called the Register the first step toward holding Russia accountable, saying it was urgent to make it operational quickly so victims could submit claims. The Register is a record-keeping body and does not itself decide on compensation. A separate claims commission and a compensation fund were planned as later steps in the mechanism.
